_read_me: The fitted relationship PA = C * Qpeak^(n-1), solved self-consistently (Qpeak depends on PA through the burst term). n=0.653 is NOT fitted here - it is carried over unchanged from melt_model.py's waveform fit against pressure TRACES (fit_model.py), an independent dataset that never saw a single PA_CALIBRATE sweep result. C is the one parameter fitted to pa_sweeps.json (13 valid rows). See docs/pa_physics.md section 5.3 for why this beats interpolating the raw grid, and section 5.4 for a competing hypothesis (pressure_advance_smooth_time attenuation) that fit the same data plausibly and was then falsified at 9.5 sigma by the accel=6000 cells. matrix[] is what was pasted into Orca's adaptive_pressure_advance_model, generated from the law rather than read off individual cells so every measurement constrains every entry. Regenerate with the solve_pa()/fit routine in this file's history (physics/fit_model.py does not yet contain it as a callable function - it was run ad hoc; formalizing it is on TODO.md).
n_source: melt_model.py waveform fit, physics/measured.json (independent of pa_sweeps.json)
C_units: PA = C * (A_fil * E_per_mm * (v_burst_peak))^(n-1), v_burst_peak in mm/s, A_fil=2.405mm^2, E_per_mm=0.046
fitted_against: physics/pa_sweeps.json, all rows with valid=true (13 rows)
blind_prediction_note: the 4 rows at accel=6000 in pa_sweeps.json were predicted by this law (fitted on the other 9) BEFORE being measured; blind chi2/dof was 0.27
